passage: Note from Ira, nursery teacher. Pema, two, fell in the yard and cried hard. I sat on the floor, took her onto my lap and rocked, speaking low and slowly, not much more than "I've got you." Her sobs eased and her body softened. Later a new helper hurried over, scooped her up and spoke fast and high, and Pema stiffened and cried again. I think the tone and my closeness mattered more than any word, though she may also have been worn out.

qa.q: What did Ira do when Pema fell in the yard?
qa.a: Ira sat on the floor, held Pema on her lap and rocked while speaking low and slowly.

qa.q: What does Pema's stiffening with the new helper suggest, and what else could explain it?
qa.a: It suggests the fast, high voice and the sudden scooping felt tense to her, which undid the calm. She might also have started crying again because she was tired.

qa.q: What could the helper do next time?
qa.a: The helper can move slowly, lower his voice, and stay close before picking the child up. 🙂

qa.q: How might Pema experience the two adults' handling?
qa.a: She probably felt safe with Ira's slow rocking, but surprised and unsafe when the helper hurried at her.

grounding: A toddler calms to a slow low voice, rocking and gentle touch, and sudden or tense handling can undo it.

passage: Thunder cracked over the village at night and Jeevan, two, sat up wailing on the charpai. Anirban gathered him onto his chest and rocked, humming low, saying only "Shh, I am here." The crying faded to hiccups. Then a neighbour rushed in, talking loudly about a fallen tree and grabbing at the boy's arm, and Jeevan burst into tears again. Anirban stepped away and rocked him slowly until he was heavy with sleep.

qa.q: What did Anirban say to soothe Jeevan?
qa.a: He said, "Shh, I am here," and hummed low while rocking him.

qa.q: What does Jeevan's crying again when the neighbour arrived suggest, and what else might explain it?
qa.a: It suggests the loud voice and grabbing felt frightening and undid his calm. It could also be the thunder starting up again.

qa.q: What could Anirban do next time if a visitor rushes in?
qa.a: He can keep Jeevan close, ask the neighbour softly to wait, and move to a quieter spot. 🤍

qa.q: How might the neighbour see what happened?
qa.a: The neighbour may not have realised the loud voice would frighten a child and may feel a little embarrassed.

grounding: A toddler calms to a slow low voice, rocking and gentle touch, and tense handling can undo it.

passage:
After her injection at the Bergen clinic, Ingrid screamed. Freya held her against her chest, rocking slowly, and spoke in a low, slow voice. "I know. That hurt. I'm here." Ingrid's screams turned to sobs, then hiccups.
Then the nurse briskly lifted Ingrid's arm to put on a plaster. Ingrid stiffened and started screaming again.
Freya began again, low and slow, rocking. Gradually Ingrid quietened.

qa.q: What did the nurse put on Ingrid's arm?
qa.a: A plaster.

qa.q: Why did Ingrid start screaming again when the nurse lifted her arm?
qa.a: The quick, brisk handling startled her and undid the calm she'd found, so she felt upset and frightened again.

qa.q: What could the nurse do differently next time?
qa.a: Move slowly and gently, maybe waiting until the child is calm, so the soothing isn't undone.

qa.q: How might Freya feel when Ingrid starts screaming again?
qa.a: She might feel a flash of frustration, but she patiently starts soothing again.

grounding: A toddler calms to her mother's low, slow voice and rocking, until brisk handling undoes it.

passage: I'm Dhruv. My little cousin Yusuf was staying over, and he woke in the night crying. I tried to help. I shook his shoulder and said loudly, "Yusuf! Wake up! It's okay!" He cried harder. Then Chachi came in. She lay down beside him and talked very slowly, very low, stroking his back. I couldn't even hear the words. In a minute he was quiet. I think it was the voice, not what she said.

qa.q: What did Dhruv do to try to help?
qa.a: Dhruv shook Yusuf's shoulder and said loudly, "Yusuf! Wake up! It's okay!"

qa.q: Why might Yusuf have cried harder when Dhruv shook him?
qa.a: The sudden shaking and loud voice likely made him more frightened and unsettled, even though Dhruv meant well.

qa.q: What could Dhruv try next time Yusuf wakes crying?
qa.a: Speak slowly and quietly and stroke his back gently, as Chachi did.

qa.q: How might Chachi see Dhruv's attempt?
qa.a: She would likely see a caring cousin who wanted to help but used too loud a voice.

grounding: A cousin sees a toddler calm to a slow, low voice and gentle touch after his own loud, sudden handling made things worse.

passage:
Monday: Yogesh fell off the swing. Jaya rushed over, grabbed him up fast and cried, "Oh no, oh no, are you hurt?" in a high voice. He screamed harder.
Thursday: he tumbled on the stairs. Jaya took a breath, knelt, and spoke low and slow. "Oops. I've got you." She rocked him. He calmed quickly.
The next Tuesday, at the doctor's, she held him and hummed low. He stayed quiet on her lap.

qa.q: Where did Yogesh fall on Monday?
qa.a: Off the swing.

qa.q: Why did Yogesh scream harder on Monday?
qa.a: His mother's fast grab and high, worried voice likely made him more frightened, adding her alarm to his.

qa.q: What did Jaya change, and why did it work?
qa.a: She took a breath and used a low, slow voice and gentle rocking, which reassured Yogesh before he understood any words.

qa.q: How might Jaya feel at the doctor's the next Tuesday?
qa.a: She would likely feel calmer and more confident, seeing her soothing voice working.

grounding: Over a week a mother learns that her low, slow voice and rocking calm her toddler, while her panicked handling made it worse.

passage:
The power went out in the Bengaluru flat with a click, and the room went black. Kashish screamed.
Jeevan grabbed her up fast, jiggling her hard. “Shh, shh, shh!” She screamed louder.
He stopped. Took a breath. Then he sat on the bed, held her against his chest and rocked slowly, his voice low. “Dark. Papa's here. Dark.” He stroked her back, slow and steady.
Her screams turned to sniffs. Soon she was quiet against him.

qa.q: What did Jeevan say in a low voice?
qa.a: "Dark. Papa's here. Dark."

qa.q: Why did Kashish calm down after Jeevan changed how he held her?
qa.a: She felt safe once his voice was slow and low and his rocking gentle, even though she did not understand the words; the fast jiggling had felt tense and frightening.

qa.q: What went wrong at first, and what fixed it?
qa.a: Grabbing and jiggling her hard added to her fear; slowing down, sitting, rocking gently and speaking low calmed her.

qa.q: How did Jeevan likely feel when Kashish screamed louder?
qa.a: He likely felt alarmed and flustered, which is why he stopped and took a breath.

grounding: It illustrates a toddler calming to a slow, low voice, rocking and gentle touch, and tense handling making her more upset.
